title: A peak-heart-rate–ST interaction gives conditional cross-hospital improvement but fails a stable incremental-prediction criterion
abstract: A fixed centered peak-heart-rate-fraction by ST-depression interaction was tested beyond flexible separate clinical/exercise measurements. Cleveland supplied303 source records; Budapest supplied294 independent hospital records. Target log loss fell0.582926 to0.567846 (difference−0.015080;conditional target bootstrap95% interval[−0.020752,−0.009639]). However, source fivefold CV worsened and source-and-target refitting yielded interval[−0.105695,+0.133951]. A linear comparator substantially outperformed the primary spline model. The prespecified stable-improvement criterion failed. This is a conditional cross-hospital comparison, not an established biomarker or clinical-utility claim. Medication confounding, historical referral populations, sparse data, missingness shift and unavailable participant linkage limit interpretation. Two isolated runs reproduced results exactly.
